Start by forming a small organizing group of five to eight reliable volunteers, including at least one person willing to coordinate schedules and one person comfortable talking with local officials or property owners. In week one, choose two or three possible sites and check sunlight, water access, soil safety, permission, and visibility from the street.

In week two, pick the site and sketch a simple layout: a few raised beds, a shared tool area, compost if allowed, and paths wide enough for easy access. Ask neighbors what they want to grow and whether they need accessible-height beds.

In week three, gather materials: soil, lumber or containers, basic tools, gloves, seeds or seedlings, and a water plan. Local businesses, schools, and garden clubs may donate supplies.

In week four, hold a build day, assign bed stewards, and set a maintenance rota. Keep rules simple: water schedule, shared harvest expectations, cleanup duties, and a monthly check-in so problems are fixed before enthusiasm fades.
